name: Super
description: Basic tech, gives the dot more horizontal momentum.
note: The overlay's SUPER JUMP: a jump in a ground dash (Movement.CheckForSuperJump). The wiki's dash jump.

name: Wallbounce
description: Basic tech, gives the dot more vertical momentum.
note: The overlay's WALL BOUNCE: the game's wallBouncePossible, an up-diagonal dash into a wall and jump (SpecialWallJump(1, …)).

name: Reverse super
description: Same as super.
note: The overlay's REVERSED SUPER: the stick points against the dash, so the super's momentum goes the stick's way.

name: Reverse super on switching block
description: I think something with coyote frames.

name: Super in switching blocks
description: The wall doesn't kill the dot because it stays in the wall too short.

name: Super in switching spikes
description: Actually the same as super in switching blocks.

name: Inwall super into wall
description: Clip in the wall like in the video, turn, do a super, turn back.

name: Inwall reverse super
description: Clip in the wall like in the video and do a reverse super.

name: Inwall super
description: Clip in the wall like in the video, then turn and turn again, and then do a super.

name: Wall clip
description: Clip in the wall, turn back and jump.

name: One spike jump
description: 1) grace frames; 2) the single spike isn't blocking one of your ground colliders; 3) the ground detectors extend down further than your hurtbox (thanks varii for the description).

name: Edge spike jump next to wall
description: Same as "One spike jump".

name: Spike wallbounce
description: Maybe the same as "One spike jump", but probably not.

name: Edge spike jump
description: Same as "One spike jump".

name: Spike super
description: Same as "One spike jump", but you do a super on the edge of the spikes.

name: Corner jump
description: There is a place on the edge of the spikes and the end of the platform where the dot can stay.

name: Buying upgrade from top
description: When you clip in a wall and dash into the wall, the dot clips a bit into it, from where you can reach the button trigger.

name: Inwall wallbounce
description: Was kind of fixed, but: when you clip in a wall and do a wallbounce on the very bottom edge of the wall, the dot clips a bit into the wall and earns vertical momentum.

name: Edge stop
description: When you clip in a wall and go backwards on the bottom edge, the dot loses all vertical momentum; probably something with coyote frames.
note: The list's own placeholder name ("it doesn't have a name").

name: Infinite mossy blocks stamina
description: When you do an inwall super into a wall, all of the dot's abilities return.

name: Gap stick
description: In a small gap the dot starts falling really slowly and pushing into the wall a bit.

name: Slope sliding
description: The dot slides down in the wall, so it can clip in a bit.

name: Checkpoint mid air jump
description: The checkpoint saves your state when you die, so you can jump in the air for a few frames when respawning.
note: Off a course, a quick restart (respawn(true)) lands where a death would: the last in-game checkpoint touched, grounded (onGround) 12 u under it. So a demo can quick-restart instead of dying. A death still ends a playback.

name: Checkpoint mid air super
description: Same as "Checkpoint mid air jump", but do a super.

name: Checkpoint mid air walljump
description: Same as "Checkpoint mid air jump", but do a walljump.

name: Up clip through slope and block
description: Jump facing the slope, turn and jump: the slope pushes the dot into the block so it can go through.

name: Fast steps slopes
description: The dot just steps up really fast many times.

name: Fast steps blocks
description: Same as "Fast steps slopes".

name: Fast steps blocks clip
description: A step is a teleport, so the dot steps and teleports up through anything.

name: Fast steps slopes glitch
description: The step teleports the dot a bit into the wall, and then jump spam doesn't kill the dot.

name: Clip through spikes
description: Only with custom spikes; nobody knows why yet.

name: Inslope wallbounce
description: Clip into a slope and do a wallbounce.

name: Spike noclip respawn
description: If the dot respawns in spikes, they don't kill it: the player never leaves the spike on death (which usually happens when they respawn).

name: Spike fall
description: Spikes aren't a place the dot can stand on, so it starts falling and the hurtbox goes a bit lower.

name: Roof squeeze
description: Spam jump for the short hitbox, so the dot can squeeze through a gap.

name: Faster acceleration
description: Turning in mid air raises the dot's acceleration from 100 units per frame to 160 units per frame.

name: Squeeze clip
description: In a small space the dot can be pushed through thin walls.

name: Dash mid air coyote jump
description: Coyote frames allow a jump in the air after a dash.

name: Momentum after quick restart
description: The dot keeps its momentum after a quick restart.

name: Pixel perfect corner boost
description: A chained diagonal dash boost that double counts momentum and sends you flying; only on corners (a maybe-pixel-perfect hyper off a corner).
note: Unconfirmed. In 100,000+ offline runs in the VMAN world, 6,787 hypers (1,673 at corners) all matched the game's formula, and none counted the pre-dash momentum twice. What players see is most likely the game's Ultra bonus, chained down ledges.

name: Ultra bonus
description: The game's own ultra (CheckForSuperJump logs "Did an ultra!"): a hyper's jump gives back all of the momentum from before the dash (preDashMomentum.x) on top of the hyper's, when the dash went the way you were moving and the jump is at least 4 u below the last hyper's or ground stay's height (lastHyperY).
note: The game calls this the ultra; the overlay's ULTRA is something else (two chained wavedashes).

name: Flip jump
description: Rising against a wall, flick the stick lightly away and back. The facing flip moves the ground rays to the other side, they hit the wall, the dot counts as grounded in mid air, and a jump on the flick back is a full ground jump. Needs no unlock (Course 1 NONE).

name: Coyote jump
description: A ground jump after the ground rays stopped hitting (coyoteFrames < maxCoyoteFrames).

name: Wall coyote jump
description: A wall jump after the wall rays stopped hitting (wallCoyoteFrames < maxWallCoyoteFrames).

name: Backwards dash-jump
description: Standing against a wall, turn away from it and press dash and jump on the same tick. The dash start moves the dot 20 u against the dash, back into the wall, and the buffered jump is a grounded dash jump from inside it.

name: Superbounce
description: Dash into a wall and press jump 0-5 ticks later: the game's dash boost, SpecialWallJump(0.6, …).

name: Wavedash
description: Omnidash (Vman): hop, dash down-diagonal, and jump in the dash. The landing turns the dash horizontal (canHyper) and the jump is the hyper (CheckForSuperJump's hyper branch).

name: Ultra
description: Omnidash (Vman): two wavedashes chained; the second dash starts in the air of the first one's jump.
note: Name clash with the game's ultra (Ultra bonus). This one gets the game's ultra only when its second hyper lands at least 4 u lower than the first. Rename or merge.

name: Dash bounce
description: Omnidash (Vman): dash straight down onto the floor and jump in the dash. The landing ends the dash with DashBounceFrames, and the jump adds dashBounceMagnitude.

name: Wave bounce
description: Omnidash (Vman): a dash bounce whose down dash started in the air of a wavedash's jump; it keeps the wavedash's speed.

name: WaveJump
description: Omnidash (Vman) with wall jump: dash up-diagonal into a wall; the dash turns straight up at full dash speed and the wall touch refills the dash.

name: Wall dash
description: Omnidash (Vman): a dash from a wall cling goes away from the wall with x set to ±1 after the normalize, so a diagonal one moves at (1670, 1181) u/s. Down-diagonal onto a floor, it becomes a wavedash off the wall.

name: Spring dash
description: A dash that cancels a sideways spring's lock.

name: Spike grace
description: Inside a spike for the ticks its graceFrames allow (up to two) without dying.
